identity.name: Nautilus Chronograph
identity.one_liner: The first Nautilus chronograph — flyback caliber with a single co-axial 60-minute and 12-hour counter.

comps.condition: similar reference: Patek Philippe 5980/1A-014 · Nautilus Chronograph

provenance_events.description: The 5980/1A is Patek's first Nautilus chronograph — a single sub-dial "small seconds"-style 60-minute counter at 6, caliber CH 28-520. The form factor becomes the basis for the future 5990 travel-time chrono.

Patek releases the 5980/1A — the first Nautilus chronograph, with the single 60-minute sub-dial layout. Hong Kong collectors treat the 5980 as the Asian-market darling: a chronograph in a steel bracelet, more wearable than the 5990 it would later spawn.

narrative.story: The 5980/1A-001 of 2006 gave the Nautilus its first chronograph, thirty years into the model's life. The flyback CH 28-520 C keeps the dial clean by stacking 60 minutes and 12 hours into one register at 6. The silver-to-black gradient of the original and the later blue-dial 5980/1A-014 both left the catalogue when Patek pulled steel Nautilus references in 2021; the chronograph continues only in gold and two-tone.
narrative.collector_notes: The -001 gradient dial and the -014 blue are distinct markets; the mono-counter takes explanation but is the reference's signature. Sticky chronograph pushers are the common service tell.
